# k3d_namespace (Resource)

A Kubernetes namespace. Creating one that already exists fails: import it instead. If a Helm chart also creates this namespace, let only one of them own it. Import with `<cluster>/<name>`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "k3d_namespace" "app" {
  cluster = k3d_cluster.main.id
  name    = "app"

  labels = {
    "istio-injection" = "enabled"
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Namespace name.

### Optional

- `annotations` (Map of String) Annotations. Only keys set here are tracked, so ones added by controllers do not show as changes.
- `cluster` (String) Cluster to manage the object in, usually `k3d_cluster.<name>.id`, so the object is recreated when the cluster is replaced. Exactly one of `cluster` or `kubeconfig` is required.
- `kubeconfig` (String, Sensitive) Kubeconfig contents, for a cluster that is reached directly and not through Docker. Not recorded as a dependency on the cluster's lifetime, so prefer `cluster` for clusters in the same configuration. It is stored in Terraform state, so use an encrypted state backend.
- `labels` (Map of String) Labels, such as `istio-injection`. Only keys set here are tracked, so ones added by controllers do not show as changes.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) `<cluster>/<name>`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import k3d_namespace.app demo/app
```
